title: Ask better questions
description: A good question is a tool: it opens doors that statements cannot. Small changes in how you ask can change what you learn.

body.heading: Open beats closed
paragraphs: Questions that can be answered with yes or no end conversations quickly. Open questions invite stories: not 'Did you like the job?' but 'What did you like about it?' Not 'Was it hard?' but 'What was the hardest part?'
Another upgrade is asking about specifics. 'How did you learn to do that?' gets a warmer, richer answer than 'Are you good at that?', because it asks about a journey rather than a judgement.

body.heading: Follow the interesting thread
paragraphs: The best second question is usually hidden inside the first answer. Listen for the detail that surprises you or that the speaker lights up about, and ask about that.
Curiosity is a compliment. People can tell the difference between genuine interest and interrogation, and it is mostly in whether you actually listen to the reply before asking the next thing.

takeaway: Ask open, specific questions, then follow the thread that lights up.
